tips.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Transnistria, which is outside the control of the Moldovan government. At the de facto checkpoints passports are controlled but not stamped, and you fill in 2 copies of a migration card and keep one to show when you leave. All border crossings between Ukraine and Transnistria are temporarily closed.

If you enter Moldova overland from Ukraine, the UK FCDO says to go to an internationally recognised border crossing point, in the north or south of Moldova, excluding the Transnistria region, and to check for updates on border crossings with the Moldovan Border Police.

The Government of Canada says credit cards are increasingly being accepted but the economy is primarily cash-based, and that only a few ATMs in Chisinau accept foreign bank cards; the UK FCDO says paying by card is now generally widespread, though not always possible, particularly outside Chisinau. The UK FCDO also says Transnistria uses the Transnistrian ruble, that the self-declared authorities consider paying there in other currencies illegal, and that ATMs in Transnistrian banks do not accept cards from non-Transnistrian banks.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Moldova?
faq.answer: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list of nationalities exempted from a visa names, among others, the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Japan, Germany, France, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Serbia, and the Border Police says foreigners may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Foreign citizens can apply online at evisa.gov.md for short-stay (type C) visas only.

faq.question: How do I get a Moldova eVisa?
faq.answer: Apply online at the government portal evisa.gov.md, which takes only short-stay (type C) visa applications; type A, B and D visas are applied for at a Moldovan diplomatic mission or consular office. The eVisa costs €40, paid by international bank card once the application is complete, and the portal says examination takes up to 10 calendar days, extendable to 20 if necessary. At the border you need the printed eVisa, your travel document, a copy of the invitation where applicable and the documents justifying the purpose of the trip, and medical insurance for the stay.

faq.question: Can I visit Transnistria?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Transnistria, which it says is outside the control of the Moldovan government. It says the de facto authorities may ask the purpose and length of your visit and where you will stay, and may deny you entry; when you enter you fill in 2 copies of a migration card and keep one to show when you leave.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Moldova without a visa?
faq.answer: The Border Police says foreigners may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counting the 180 days before each day of stay. The UK FCDO says you need a work or residence permit to work or for stays of more than 90 days.

faq.question: Is Moldova in the EU or the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: The European Commission says the Schengen area is composed of 29 countries: 25 EU member states and 4 non-EU countries (Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein).
